explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "The Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it…" (Numbers 2:2). Six hundred thousand men and a whole lot of families, and every tent is arranged around one spot. Nobody has to ask where the middle is.

Good guess, friend, but that's not what the LORD names here. In this passage He says the Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 2:2). The altar doesn't come up at all in these verses. So when the camp looks toward its middle, the Tent of Meeting is what's sitting there.

The pillar of cloud, friend? It never shows up in these verses. What the LORD says is, "The Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it…" (Numbers 2:2). So every family gets a spot around that one center. I can barely get my six cookie cutter kids to line up on one counter, so this is impressive.

Close, friend, but no. The LORD says they camp "…at a distance from it…" (Numbers 2:2). That means space, not tent flaps rubbing up against the Tent of Meeting. Picture a crowd that leaves some room around the middle instead of piling in on top of it.

You've got it, baker! The text says the Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting "…at a distance from it…" (Numbers 2:2). So nobody is pitching a tent against it. They circle around it and leave room in between.

Yes, baker! "On the east side, toward the sunrise, the divisions of Judah are to camp under their standard…" (Numbers 2:3). Issachar camps next to them, then Zebulun (Numbers 2:5, 7). And Judah's camp sets out first (Numbers 2:9). Sunrise side AND first out the door? I would've asked for the west side and a long nap.

Reuben's a good name to land on, friend, but they're not on the east. The text puts "…the divisions of Reuben…" on the south side (Numbers 2:10). The east, toward the sunrise, belongs to Judah (Numbers 2:3). Each tribe has its own spot, so it pays to keep the directions straight.

Not this time, baker. Dan camps on the north side (Numbers 2:25), so Dan isn't who the sunrise greets. The east side, toward the sunrise, is for Judah (Numbers 2:3). Dan shows up later in the plan, so hang onto that name.

That's right, baker. The camp of Judah, 186,400 men in all, "…shall set out first." (Numbers 2:9). They camp on the east and they lead the way when Israel moves. When the whole camp starts rolling, Judah is out front.

Second belongs to somebody else, friend. The camp of Reuben, with 151,450 men, is the one that "…shall set out second." (Numbers 2:16). Judah's camp, 186,400 men, goes before them. The LORD gives each camp its turn in line.
Last is a different camp, baker. The camp of Dan, with 157,600 men, "…shall set out last…" (Numbers 2:31). Judah's 186,400 men go first (Numbers 2:9). Judah and Dan are the two ends of the line.

Exactly, baker! "In the middle of the camps, the Tent of Meeting is to travel with the camp of the Levites." (Numbers 2:17). It isn't out front, and it isn't dragging at the back. The camps set out "…in the order they encamped, each in his own place under his standard." (Numbers 2:17). Everybody gets a spot, and the Tent gets the middle one.

Judah has a big job, friend, but it's a different one. They set out first (Numbers 2:9). The Tent of Meeting travels "…with the camp of the Levites." in the middle of the camps (Numbers 2:17). Judah leads the way, and the Levites carry the middle.

That's a new name for this passage, baker. These verses never mention the seventy elders. What they say is that the Tent of Meeting "…is to travel with the camp of the Levites." (Numbers 2:17). The Levites keep the middle.

You got it, baker. The LORD says, "They are to set out in the order they encamped, each in his own place under his standard." (Numbers 2:17). Nobody has to figure out a new arrangement on moving day. The way they camp is the way they march.

Actually it's true, friend. The text says, "They are to set out in the order they encamped, each in his own place under his standard." (Numbers 2:17). So there's no reshuffling when it's time to go. Each tribe keeps its place in the order.

That's the one, baker. "On the north side, the divisions of Dan are to camp under their standard…" (Numbers 2:25). East, south and west are already handed out, so north is what's left. Dan, Asher and Naphtali fill it.

The middle is already taken, friend. The Tent of Meeting travels there "…with the camp of the Levites." (Numbers 2:17). The last group of tribes goes on the north side (Numbers 2:25). The middle is the center, not one of the four sides.

East has its own crowd, baker. Judah, Issachar and Zebulun camp there, toward the sunrise (Numbers 2:3-8). The LORD puts the last tribes on the north side (Numbers 2:25). No one gets sent out past the edge of the plan.

Close, baker, but not quite. The camp of Dan does set out last (Numbers 2:31). The Tent of Meeting, though, travels "In the middle of the camps…" with the Levites (Numbers 2:17). It's tucked between the camps, not dragging along behind everybody.

Yes, baker! Dan does set out last (Numbers 2:31), but the Tent of Meeting travels "In the middle of the camps…" (Numbers 2:17). So the Tent isn't at the back at all. Dan's camp is the one bringing up the rear. It's an easy mix-up, since "last" sounds like it covers everybody.

Not quite, friend. The text says, "But the Levites were not counted among the other Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 2:33). The 603,550 is "The total of those counted in the camps, by their divisions…" (Numbers 2:32). The Levites aren't in that number, even though they travel with the Tent.

Right, baker! The total of 603,550 is "The total of those counted in the camps, by their divisions…" (Numbers 2:32), and the Levites aren't in it. "But the Levites were not counted among the other Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 2:33). Over six hundred thousand men counted, and one whole tribe sits out of the number on purpose. That's a lot of counting, and I'd have lost my place around number forty.

That's it, baker. "So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses…" (Numbers 2:34). Every tribe camped under its standard, and they set out the same way, each man with his clan and his family. All of it was followed.

explanations.answer: They follow only part of it
explanations.explanation: The text says more than that, friend. "So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses…" (Numbers 2:34). Not most of it. Everything. I've followed a recipe "mostly" before, and the cookies let me know about it. Here, they camped under their standards in this way and set out in the same way, each man with his clan and his family.

explanations.answer: They swap a few of the spots
explanations.explanation: Nobody's trading places in this passage, baker. The text says the Israelites "…camped under their standards in this way and set out in the same way…" (Numbers 2:34). Each man stayed with his clan and his family. The spots stayed just as the LORD gave them.
